\begin{tablenotes}[flushleft]
\footnotesize
\item \textit{Notes:} Panel A: each row re-estimates Ho et al.'s factor-augmenting model, $\log\text{ppl}=E_b+A_b e^{-\alpha g_N t}N^{-\alpha}+B_b e^{-\beta g_D t}D^{-\beta}$, under the stated restriction (L1-penalized rows other than A1 are run to convergence); $g_N$, $g_D$ are augmentation rates (log points per year), $T_C=\ln 2/(g_N+g_D)$ the effective-compute doubling time, $\gamma=\alpha\beta/(\alpha+\beta)$. Intervals: 95\% paper-cluster bootstrap (400 draws), mapped from the distribution of $g_N+g_D$ ($\infty$ when non-positive growth is inside the interval; $g_C<0$: the point estimate implies that effective compute \emph{fell}). Hicks neutrality is $\alpha g_N=\beta g_D$. Experimental $\gamma$ in total-loss units is the frontier elasticity obtained by fitting Ho's $E=0$ form to the Chinchilla sweep (0.0525). Row A6 does not re-estimate: it divides Ho's year coefficients by Besiroglu et al.'s exponents (Whitfill 2025). Panel B: $\overline{CE}$ is the geometric mean of Farrell cost efficiency $C_{\min}(L^T(N,D))/6ND$ under a fixed technology $T$ (allocative only; $E$ and loss units cancel). Allocative gain $=\overline{CE}_{2022\text{--}24}/\overline{CE}_{2020\text{--}21}$ with a bootstrap over models (and, for Besiroglu, over technology draws). Ho-rate gain $=\exp(g_C\Delta t)$ with Ho et al.'s point estimate and $\Delta t$ the difference in mean release dates; allocative share $=\ln(\text{allocative gain})/\ln(\text{Ho-rate gain})$. Cleaned sample: drops instruct/chat/vision-language derivatives, systems-paper runs, non-transformer and molecular models, exact re-releases (same organization, $N$, $C$), models with $D/N$ exactly 20 (possibly imputed) and Epoch `speculative' entries.
\end{tablenotes}
\end{threeparttable}
